subject: Locality Assurance, Failover Orchestration & Subprocessor Transparency
messages:
From: Tom Levin <tom.levin@helixcare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Locality commitments + transient analytic bursts

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this early call. As we proceed toward procurement review, a couple of items we need clarified for the DPA and technical onboarding:

- Can Redwood provide a firm commitment that customer production data for HelixCare accounts will be anchored to the EU region (AWS eu-west-1) for at-rest storage and primary inference?
- What is your documented policy for transient cross-region processing for analytics/troubleshooting (e.g., temporary burst to US regions)? We need a written maximum window and triggers.
- Please share the current subprocessors roster and whether any analytics pipelines will route tokens outside the EU for aggregation.
- Will you accept an addendum that limits transient processing to incident response and scheduled maintenance only?

We attached our DPA questions worksheet to help focus the legal review. Happy to hop on a short call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Levin
Head of Privacy, HelixCare
privacy-team@helixcare.com

Attachment: HelixCare_DPA_Questions.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Levin <tom.levin@helixcare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Locality commitments + transient analytic bursts

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, with a proposed next step.

1) Local anchoring: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we can anchor production data to EU (eu-west-1) and restrict egress. For Hosted customers we offer EU tenancy options; we'll provide a formal Locality Assurance Annex to capture the scope.

2) Transient cross-region processing: We operate an incident-driven and workload-driven policy. We are prepared to commit to:
   - a documented transient window of up to 48 hours for emergency debugging and root-cause analytics;
   - scheduled maintenance bursts (pre-authorized) with prior notice;
   - any transient processing must be logged and is subject to audit via our telemetry exports.

3) Subprocessors: We'll provide a current roster and indicate which subprocessors are used for telemetry/analytics vs inference serving.

4) DPA addendum: We can accept an addendum that constrains transient processing to incident response and defined maintenance windows, subject to mutually agreed notification and audit procedures.

Next steps — I attached a short Locality Annex draft that outlines the anchor + transient window language and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP). Ben, can you pick up scheduling for a 30-minute call with Helix legal this week?

— Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Locality_Annex_Draft.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tom Levin <tom.levin@helixcare.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Locality commitments + transient analytic bursts — Legal clarifications and proposed DPA language

Tom / Monica / Ben / Grace —

Following the thread and internal review, a few legal clarifications and proposed language for the DPA addendum:

1) Scope of anchoring: We can include an explicit clause that production customer data will be "anchored" to EU (eu-west-1) for storage, inference cache residency, and primary telemetry capture for HelixCare accounts when the customer selects the EU tenancy option (Dedicated or Private). This will be reflected in the annex.

2) Transient processing window: We recommend making the transient window explicit and auditable. Proposed language: "Redwood may conduct transient, non-production processing of HelixCare customer data outside the EU strictly for incident response, troubleshooting, or scheduled maintenance; such processing shall not exceed 48 continuous hours per incident without prior written approval from HelixCare and shall be logged and exported to HelixCare's telemetry endpoint."

3) Analytics subprocessors: We will provide the active subprocessors CSV and flag any vendor that performs aggregation/analytics. For any subprocessor that would process data outside the EU, we will include an extra attestation and a 30-day notice prior to activation for HelixCare.

4) Audit and evidence: We can commit to providing audit logs and a monthly transient-processing report for the first 90 days post-go-live.

If HelixCare is comfortable with the proposed wording above, we will prepare a tracked addendum. Otherwise, please propose alternate language.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: subprocessors_current_roster.csv (text/csv, stub)
